---
title: "Predictive modeling of claims status"
author: 'Satvik Talchuru'
date: 11/17/2025
---

### Abstract

We developed a predictive model for classifying webpages into “relevant claim content’’ vs. “no relevant content’’ using the cleaned text provided in `claims-clean-example.RData`. We represented page text using TF–IDF and trained a LASSO logistic regression model for the binary classification task. This model achieved strong performance with cross-validated accuracy comparable to in-class PCA logistic regression benchmarks. Multiclass modeling was not performed for this project, so multiclass results are not applicable.

### Preprocessing

The visible text, including header content and paragraph text, was taken from the raw HTML. After eliminating markup, punctuation, stopwords, and standardizing to lowercase, this text was cleaned. Then, the cleansed text was tokenized into word tokens and transformed into a sparse term-document matrix. Using TF–IDF weighting, we generated quantitative feature representations with tens of thousands of distinct tokens that were appropriate for machine learning. The held-out test pages were preprocessed using the same vocabulary and TF–IDF transformer.

### Methods

We employed a LASSO logistic regression model ('glmnet') for the binary classification assignment. We used TF–IDF characteristics from the training dataset as input to a cross-validated penalized logistic regression model. Because it automatically selects features, the L1 penalty (alpha = 1) is ideal for sparse text data in high dimensions. Using cross-validation, the tuning parameter that reduced the misclassification rate was automatically chosen (`lambda.min`). On the test set, the last model was used to predict class probabilities, which were then thresholded at 0.5 to create binary class predictions. No model was trained for the multiclass job. As a result, the metrics and predictions for several classes were not relevant for this submission.
